title.narrative: Technical assistance for the early recovery of the province of Pinar del Río, Cuba, through a program to strengthen capacities for the protection and right to adequate housing of people affected by hurricane Ian.

description.narrative:
The project described below will focus on supporting local institutions in territorial planning and technical assistance to carry out an efficient and effective response and early recovery process after hurricane Ian. The greatest damage is concentrated in the municipalities of Consolación del Sur, La Palma, San Luis, San Juan y Martínez, Pinar del Río, Viñales and Los Palacios, which add up to more than 80 % of the total damages to homes and more than 95 % referred to the total collapse of houses and roofs.
Of the 7 most affected municipalities that will be considered in the project, four of them are already working on the implementation of the New Urban Agenda, they are Consolación del Sur, San Juan y Martínez, Pinar del Río and Viñales (for previous technical assistance from UN-Habitat).
The general objective of the project is to support the early recovery of seven municipalities of Pinar del Río through capacity building programs to reestablish the right to adequate housing for the people affected by hurricane Ian.
The project has a duration of one year and responds to Action Plan for emergency prepared by United Nations System in Cuba to provide technical assistance on the right to adequate housing, strengthening of local technical capacities in urban planning and protection of urban heritage.
The technical scope of the collaboration includes:
• Technical support to strengthen the local capacities and the procedures offices to allow the urban legal processes in the recovery of the housing sector. • To strengthen productive capacities in the municipality of Viñales through capacity building processes to public and private entrepreneurs and roofers to produce the creole tiles involved in the reconstruction of homes, in accordance with the criteria of the World Heritage.
The project considers integrating a gender approach in the process. The participation of women is a priority and will be considered during the development of the technical assistance.
The project will build on and apply global tools and methodologies already developed by UN-Habitat. These methodologies and lessons learned are described in detail in section 2.3, however, due to their relevance they are detailed below:
• URBAN RECOVERY FRAMEWORK, UN-Habitat 2022 • Planning Law Assessment Framework. UN-Habitat, 2016. • Slum Upgrading Legal Assessment Framework, UN-Habitat, 2022. • Urban Law Module of the Law and Climate Change Toolkit, 2022. • Participatory Incremental Urban Planning Toolbox (Our City Plans): A Toolbox to support local governments in developing countries to implement the New Urban Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. UN-Habitat 2020. • Human Rights, Rule of Law and the New Urban Agenda. UN-Habitat, 2020.
